text: A possible family group of techniques is the poor error correction codes, and we made the example of the repetition code. Very simple, and it's what we do—we humans do—to repeat information whenever the receiver is not able to understand correctly. The second type of technique that we are going to discuss today is ARQ—Automatic Repeat Retransmission Request. Okay. This is what we are going to explain in a minute. But what we already said yesterday is that in this second case, we handle bits grouped into packets. Okay. So we do not look at the single bits, but we look at a group of bits that are carried into a packet. And the packet we said is like a message—an email that we send, right? And the single bits are like the letters that we write in a message—in the email message. Okay. So we send a packet from a transmitter.
